title: Larkspur SE field notes - pre-onsite
body:
Context:
Larkspur (retail analytics customer) — evaluating Redwood Private on their Azure tenancy with a dedicated VPC-to-VNet model. Onsite next week: Nov 13–14. Goal is to confirm network/ops constraints, sizing, and a minimal proof-of-concept deploy plan that hits their latency target (<= 120ms p95 for short prompts) and complies with their security checklist.

High-level plan / deliverables for onsite:
- Day 1: architecture review + network validation + quick demo using hosted model fallback.
- Day 2: validate Dedicated capacity sizing, run a simple inference test against their sample workload, hand off runbook and next-step backlog.

Quick notes from pre-call (11/07) with Larkspur infra team:
- They have strict egress controls: only outbound to our control-plane IPs allowed via NATGW.
- No cross-tenant peering; must use Private Link equivalent (Azure Private Endpoint) or set up express route to our VPC.
- HSM/KMS: key policies restrict key usage to tenant-managed principals. We can integrate via customer KMS but need instructions from their security team.
- Compliance: logs must be forwarded to their SIEM (Splunk) over TLS on port 8088.

Immediate technical checklist (things to confirm onsite):
- IP allowlist for control plane and fallback endpoints — get CIDR list and bring printed copy.
- Confirm whether they permit ephemeral outbound connections to model update endpoints (for model catalog sync). If not, we need to bundle model artifacts ahead of time.
- Verify subnet sizing: need /26 minimum per GPU pool (estimate) for management + worker nodes. Confirm overlapping CIDR warning with their existing infra.
- Confirm NAT GW throughput and any egress throttling schedules (nightly batch jobs).
- KMS/HSM onboarding: get contact + Vault path + sample policy.

Sizing assumptions (rough, for discussion):
- Target: 1M tokens/day, peak concurrency ~120 rps, typical prompt length ~60 tokens.
- Starting plan: 4x A10G-equivalent GPU workers in Dedicated pool with burst headroom to 8 for spikes. (Rationale: predictable latency; can downscale after evaluation).
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for chat flows — expect 20–30% token cost saving.

Commands/ops notes to try during demo:
- Validate connectivity from their VNet to our private endpoint: 
  $ az network private-endpoint show --name redwood-pe --resource-group RG-Larkspur
- Test outbound to control plane IPs (from jump host): 
  $ curl -v https://control.redwood-inference.com/healthz --resolve control.redwood-inference.com:443:52.10.12.34
- Small inference smoke test (post-deploy): 
  $ curl -X POST https://private.redwood/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
(we'll have a temporary token for demo)

Open questions / risks to call out:
- If model catalog sync is blocked, using static pinned model artifacts increases operational overhead for updates. Need to confirm acceptable cadence for manual updates.
- KMS integration delays could block automated key rotation; fallback is to use customer-provided encrypted secrets and rotate keys manually.
- Their SIEM requires a specific TLS cipher suite and mutual TLS — verify their Splunk forwarder config.

Action items (owner, due):
- Priya: prepare minimal Terraform module for Private Endpoint + route table example; include notes for /26 recommendation. (Due: 2024-11-11)
- Ethan: assemble CIDR allowlist and control-plane IPs; get approval from networking. (Due: 2024-11-09)
- Maya: draft runbook sections for KMS onboarding and for Splunk forwarder configuration; include rollback steps. (Due: 2024-11-11)
- Priya/Ethan: create demo dataset (10 sample user queries + expected output) and load into Larkspur test tenant. (Due: 2024-11-12)
- Priya: print checklist for onsite: ID badges, signed NDA, NAT GW screenshots, KMS contact cards. (Due: 2024-11-12)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep demo short: show cold-start latency, cache-hit improvement, and a canary failover to hosted API. Don't deep-dive into quantization unless they ask.
- If asked about cost, show per-token breakdown and how caching/ batching reduces it. Bring two slides: cost baseline vs optimized.
- Bring a local copy of model artifacts (quantized and FP16) in case network pulls fail. Label clearly with model name + sha.

Config snippets to attach later (placeholders):
- Terraform: azurerm_private_endpoint, azurerm_subnet, route_table for peering
- Sample YAML: agent-forwarder.yaml -> splunk_hec_token, tls: mTLS true/false

Meeting prep checklist (day-of):
- Printouts: network diagram, CIDR map, temporary token instructions
- Demo laptop: cleared, local model artifacts on external SSD, offline fallback CLI tools
- Slack channel created: #se-larkspur (already created, invite: ethan, maya, lucy-sec)

Loose observations from their infra notes:
- They run heavy ETL windows between 02:00–04:00 UTC; prefer any non-critical updates outside that window.
- They use strict tagging/inventory; ask for subscription ID early so we can pre-create resources for demo.

End of notes. Will consolidate into PRD-ish demo runbook tomorrow and attach terraform snippets.

-- Priya
